newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu wants more defence spending.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu wants more defence spending.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday Israel would have to increase its defence budget even as it tried to reduce government spending.

Netanyahu made the remark a week after announcing a second cut in Israel's 1997 budget proposal. Finance ministry sources have said the Treasury planned to present a proposal for defence cuts to the government early next month.

"I think we'll need...to allocate more money -- maybe in terms of the percentage of the GNP -- to the defence establishment until we reach the defence and security levels that I view as necessary both to attain peace and preserve it," Netanyahu told journalists in Tel Aviv.
He said there had been a certain erosion in the allocation of resources for defence and the increase was necessary for strengthening national security.
Defence spending accounts for around 16 percent of the government's 1997 proposed budget which parliament must pass by December 31. Netanyahu did not say when he would seek the increase.

He and Finance Minister Dan Meridor have proposed a seven billion shekel cut in next year's budget to narrow a spiralling budget deficit but Netanyahu has promised the cuts would not affect defence spending.
Members of the prime minister's own coalition have vowed to fight the cuts which they say target the poor.

The Haaretz newspaper said that Netanyahu, who ousted a left-centre government in elections last May, had slammed his Labour party predecessors Shimon Peres and Ytizhak Rabin for viewing peace treaties as an alternative to military prowess.

The former Labour government led Israel to breakthrough peace treaties with the Palestinians and Jordan but regional tensions have been reignited since Netanyahu was elected on a platform that rejects trading land for peace with the Arabs.

Netanyahu's decision to open a second entrance to an archaeological tunnel near a Moslem shrine in Jerusalem two months ago led to clashes with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza in which 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis were killed.

On its northern front, Israel has had to keep its army on high alert since Syria moved thousands of its troops in Lebanon to within striking range of the Golan Heights. The redeployment and a series of Syrian military exercises across the border have given Israelis war jitters.
The Haaretz newspaper said Netanyahu was also concerned about Iran's arsenal of long-range surface-to-surface missiles and its alleged efforts to build a nuclear bomb.
